correctness.rationale: The published symmetric joint-state system, with \(\gamma,\gamma_2>0\), reduces at \(\tau=\gamma\) and \(\alpha=2\gamma_2/\gamma\) to the displayed polynomial vector field. All faces of the physical triangle have inward-pointing fluxes. The identity \(Z=u+3v/2\), \(dZ/ds=-v(u+2hv)\), and LaSalle prove global extinction because \(v=0\) with \(u>0\) is not invariant. For every nonzero state, exact quotient equations for \(q=v/Z\) and \(r=v/Z^2\) yield \(q\to0\) and \(r\to1/h\). Then \(d(Z^{-2})/ds=2r(u/Z+2hv/Z)\to2/h\), giving both physical-time amplitudes. Direct symbolic checks confirm the vector field, boundary fluxes, Lyapunov identity and quotient equations. Fifteen numerical integrations are only corroborative; they are not substitutes for the infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The equalities \(\tau=\gamma\) and \(\alpha=2\gamma_2/\gamma\) are the naturally identified degenerate transition boundary of a recently published model, so the global dynamical outcome and relaxation are mathematically motivated. An exact Lyapunov function excludes persistent positive states for all \(h=\gamma_2/\gamma>0\), and the distinct observable tails \(u(t)\asymp t^{-1/2}\) and \(v(t)\asymp t^{-1}\) separate single from double infection. The precise leading amplitude \(v(t)\sim1/(2\gamma t)\) is independent of \(\gamma_2\) at this tuned boundary. These are natural system-level invariants, not a renaming, known-table recomputation, or an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
